title: Bartholomew's Splashy Secret
markdown:
Bartholomew Bumble was a goat who felt quite a lot of pride. Not the show-off kind, mind you. His pride was a quiet, steady thing, like a strong root. He was the keeper of the prize-winning rose garden at Willow Creek Public Gardens, and oh, how those roses bloomed! Each soft petal showed how well he looked after them. His gardening was so good, it was like a beautiful song of red, pink, and yellow flowers. Bartholomew had a secret, though, a little knot of worry he kept hidden like a seed in winter. While he could spot a plant disease from far away and trim a thorny stem with perfect care, there was one thing he disliked more than slugs on a young plant: being wrong. Especially in front of important people. It made his whiskers droop and his tail twitch in a way that made him feel all uncomfortable.

His best friend in all the world, who helped him when his pride got a bit too much, was Nell. Nell was a tortoise whose shell was the color of old moss, with swirls and lines that looked like they’d been drawn by the wind. She moved slowly and carefully, like the sun coming up. Nell saw the world slowly, and she understood Bartholomew's pride. She knew it was like a garden that just needed a little sunshine, not a big storm. "You worry too much, Barty," she'd often say, her voice a soft rumble like pebbles shifting in a dry creek bed.

"Ah, but here's the thing, Nell," Bartholomew would say, fixing a rose leaf with his neat hoof. "A gardener's good name is as delicate as a butterfly's wing. One wrong word, one misplaced garden tool, and it's all ruined!" He'd shudder dramatically, his horns gleaming in the dappled sunlight.

One bright Tuesday morning, the air in the usually peaceful garden office buzzed with hushed excitement. Bartholomew was pretending to look closely at a ladybug when he heard the head gardener mumble to himself. "Mr. Sterling, the important inspector, is coming this week. He's seen gardens all over the place! If he likes our roses, it'll be great for everyone!"

Bartholomew’s ears perked up, swiveling like little antennas. Mr. Sterling! The very same Mr. Sterling who had once, in his famously sharp voice, called a perfectly nice marigold a "plain, but not very exciting, bit of color." Bartholomew had felt a prickle of annoyance then, and he felt it again now, even stronger. This was his chance! His chance to show that his garden was the very best, and that *he* was perfect. But to do that, he knew he needed more than just perfect roses. He needed to seem calm and collected. He needed to look like he never made any mistakes. A gardener who was so calm and in control that anyone looking would see not one tiny mistake, but a perfect, peaceful expert.

"Nell, my dear," Bartholomew announced, puffing out his chest and trying to look casual, though his eyes sparkled with determination. "I think we need to go for a special trip. To the Willow Creek Public Baths. A nice, calm swim, you see, to help me feel very peaceful and in charge. A cool dip to make me feel sharp and smooth out any… worries."

Nell blinked slowly, her old eyes taking in everything Bartholomew said. "The baths, Barty? Are you sure that will help your roses? They don't seem to be wilting."

"It will help *me*, Nell! And a calm gardener does the best work. Mr. Sterling needs to see me as the most relaxed person. We must look… *amazing*." Bartholomew practiced a grand nod, and almost tumbled over.

So, Bartholomew Bumble, with his neatly combed goat hair (he'd even put a bit of rose-scented oil in it!) and a determined sparkle in his eye that wasn't calm at all, trotted towards the sparkling blue swimming baths. Nell, as always, followed along faithfully, a quiet shadow of wisdom. Bartholomew imagined himself gliding through the water, looking graceful and smooth, like a swan on a calm lake. He pictured Mr. Sterling seeing him, nodding and maybe even saying, "Ah, what a calm person."

He stayed in the shallow end, of course. Deep water was too unpredictable and could cause sudden, embarrassing splashes. He dipped a hoof in carefully, then another, trying to move with the slow, smooth style he thought important inspectors would have. He even tried a little side stroke, which mostly meant wobbling and trying not to notice his own awkward splashes that made waves on the calm water. Meanwhile, Nell had found a sunny spot on a big, fluffy towel by the edge, happily soaking up the warmth. Bartholomew was just starting to feel a little bit calm and confident, when...

*SPLASH!*

A child, maybe about eight years old, let out a happy yell and cannonballed into the water just a few lanes away. The splash was so big, it sent a huge wave of water towards Bartholomew. The cold water shocked him, stinging his eyes. His carefully practiced calm vanished like mist on a warm day. He sputtered and coughed, flailing his hooves wildly, trying to get his balance. In his panic, he did a rather clumsy roll, and his precious gardening shears (he always carried them, just in case a rose needed a quick trim!) clattered onto the floor.

And then he saw him. Standing by the edge, wiping his glasses with a clean white handkerchief, Mr. Sterling looked perfectly dry and calm. A small, amused smile touched his lips, and his eyes crinkled a little. Bartholomew felt his face turn a bright red, a color that would have made even his brightest roses look pale. He, Bartholomew Bumble, the perfect gardener, had just splashed about like a silly toy in front of the famous Mr. Sterling. Oh, how embarrassing!

He scrambled out of the water, dripping and feeling awful, his rose-scented oil washing away. Nell slowly walked towards him, her steady walk making him feel a little better.

"Oh, Barty," she said softly, her old eyes understanding. "Sometimes, it's much better to just be honest. Trying to be a graceful swan when you're a goat who just got splashed... it only makes it feel worse when you fall, doesn't it?"

Bartholomew, his pride hurting more than the watery sting, hung his head, his wet fur sticking to him. "I... I wanted to impress him, Nell. I hate being wrong. I hate looking silly. I thought if I looked totally calm, he'd think I was the best gardener ever."

Just then, Mr. Sterling walked over, his smile growing wider. "Mr. Bumble, I assume? That's a very interesting way you have of pruning in the water." He chuckled, a warm, real sound that surprised Bartholomew. "Don't worry, my friend. I've been trying to impress people with my garden since I was a kid. I've learned that real confidence isn't about never making a mistake, but about how you deal with it when you do. And," he winked, pointing to Bartholomew’s wet shears, "I've always found a good laugh can solve more problems than a perfect petal. I once tried to look very calm before a big garden show by standing on my head. It didn't end well. My marigolds, though, were amazing, even though I was upside down for a while. Maybe you're just as tough with your own plants?"

Bartholomew looked at Mr. Sterling, then at Nell, who gave him a slow, encouraging nod, her shell shining in the sun. He felt a weight lift from his shoulders, a feeling much better than any cold swim. He wasn't perfect, and that was... okay. It was more than okay.

"Thank you, Mr. Sterling," Bartholomew said, a small, real smile finally appearing on his goat lips. It felt much better than trying to look perfect. "I guess... I guess I have a lot to learn about being a truly great gardener. And about swimming baths, it seems." He even managed a little laugh, a wobbly but honest sound.

As Mr. Sterling walked away, waving his handkerchief at the man polishing the diving board, Bartholomew looked at his wet shears, then back at his best friend. "You know, Nell," he said, a new sparkle in his eye that was much nicer than his old worried look, "maybe my roses will grow even better with a little… unexpected water." And maybe," he added, nudging her gently with his nose, showing he cared, "I'm not so bad at being wrong after all. Especially when I have friends like you to remind me it's okay to be a bit wobbly sometimes."

And that's the funny thing about pride, my dear child. Sometimes, the biggest win isn't about never falling, but about learning to get back up, dripping but smiling, with a friend beside you and a good story to share. And Bartholomew Bumble, the proud gardener, realized that day that sometimes, the most important thing to grow wasn't just perfect roses, but a happy heart.
characters: observant goat gardener, tortoise friend Nell
audience: children aged 11-12, amusing story for older children
author: StoryGen Community
